chapters.title_en: The Introduction: On the Name of the Book and Its Division into Premises and Poles
chapters.arabic_text:
### | بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم

الحمد لله الذي اجتبى من صفوة عباده عصابة الحق وأهل السنة، وخصهم من بين
سائر الفرق بمزايا اللطف والمنة، وأفاض عليهم من نور هدايته ما كشف به عن
حقائق الدين، وأنطق ألسنتهم بحجته التي قمع بها ضلال الملحدين، وصفى
سرائرهم من وساوس الشياطين، وطهر ضمائرهم عن نزغات الزائغين، وعمر أفئدتهم
بأنوار اليقين حتى اهتدوا بها إلى أسرار ما أنزله على لسان نبيه وصفيه محمد
صلى الله عليه وسلم سيد المرسلين، واطلعوا على طريق التلفيق بين مقتضيات
الشرائع وموجبات العقول؛ وتحققوا أن لا معاندة بين الشرع المنقول والحق
المعقول. وعرفوا أن من ظن من الحشوية وجوب الجمود على التقليد، واتباع
الظواهر ما أتوا به إلا من ضعف العقول وقلة البصائر. وإن من تغلغل من
الفلاسفة وغلاة المعتزلة في تصرف العقل حتى صادموا به قواطع الشرع، ما أتوا
به إلا من خبث الضمائر. فميل أولئك إلى التفريط وميل هؤلاء إلى الافراط،
وكلاهما بعيد عن الحزم والاحتياط. بل الواجب المحتوم في قواعد الاعتقاد
ملازمة الاقتصاد والاعتماد على الصراط المستقيم؛ فكلا طرفي قصد الأمور
ذميم. وأنى يستتب الرشاد لمن يقنع بتقليد
الأثر والخبر، وينكر مناهج البحث والنظر، أو لا يعلم انه لا مستند للشرع
إلا قول سيد البشر صلى الله عليه وسلم، وبرهان العقل هو الذي عرف به صدقه
فيما أخبر، وكيف يهتدي للصواب من اقتفى محض العقل واقتصر، وما استضاء بنور
الشرع ولا استبصر؟ فليت شعري كيف يفزع إلى العقل من حيث يعتريه العي
والحصر؟ أو لا يعلم ان العقل قاصر وأن مجاله ضيق منحصر؟ هيهات قد خاب على
القطع والبتات وتعثر بأذيال الضلالات من لم يجمع بتأليف الشرع والعقل هذا
الشتات. فمثال العقل البصر السليم عن الآفات والاذاء. ومثال القرآن الشمس
المنتشرة الضياء. فاخلق بأن يكون طالب الاهتداء. المستغني إذا استغني
بأحدهما عن الآخر في غمار الأغبياء، فالمعرض عن العقل مكتفيا بنور القرآن،
مثاله المتعرض لنور الشمس مغمضا للأجفان، فلا فرق بينه وبين العميان.
فالعقل مع الشرع نور  على نور، والملاحظ بالعين العور لأحدهما على الخصوص
متدل بحبل غرور. وسيتضح لك أيها المشوق إلى الاطلاع على قواعد عقائد أهل
السنة، المقترح تحقيقها بقواطع الأدلة، أنه لم يستأثر بالتوفيق للجمع بين
الشرع والتحقيق فريق سوى هذا الفريق. فاشكر الله تعالى على إقتفائك لآثارهم
وانخراطك في سلك نظامهم وعيارهم واختلاطك بفرقتهم؛ فعساك أن تحشر يوم
القيامة في زمرتهم. نسأل الله تعالى أن يصفي أسرارنا عن كدورات الضلال،
ويغمرها بنور الحقيقة، وأن يخرس ألسنتنا عن النطق بالباطل، وينطقها بالحق
والحكمة إنه الكريم الفائض المنة الواسع الرحمة.

### | باب

ولنفتح الكلام ببيان اسم الكتاب، وتقسيم المقدمات والفصول والأبواب. أما
اسم الكتاب فهو الاقتصاد في الاعتقاد. وأما ترتيبه فهو مشتمل على أربع
تمهيدات تجري مجرى التوطئة والمقدمات، وعلى أربع أقطاب تجري مجرى المقاصد
والغايات.

### | التمهيد الأول: في بيان أن

هذا العلم من المهمات في الدين.
التمهيد الثاني: في بيان أنه ليس مهما لجميع المسلمين بل لطائفة منهم
مخصوصين.
التمهيد الثالث: في بيان أنه من فروض الكفايات لا من فروض الأعيان.
التمهيد الرابع: في تفصيل مناهج الأدلة التي أوردتها في هذا الكتاب.
وأما الأقطاب المقصودة فأربعة وجملتها مقصورة على النظر في الله تعالى.
فإنا إذا نظرنا في العالم لم ننظر فيه من حيث أنه عالم وجسم وسماء وأرض، بل
من حيث
أنه صنع الله سبحانه. وإن نظرنا في النبي عليه السلام لم ننظر فيه من حيث
أنه انسان وشريف وعالم وفاضل؛ بل من حيث أنه رسول الله. وان نظرنا في
أقواله لم ننظر من حيث أنها أقوال ومخاطبات وتفهيمات؛ بل من حيث أنها
تعريفات بواسطته من الله تعالى، فلا نظر إلا في الله ولا مطلوب سوى الله
وجميع أطراف هذا العلم يحصرها النظر في ذات الله تعالى وفي صفاته سبحانه
وفي أفعاله عز وجل وفي رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وما جاءنا على لسانه
من تعريف الله تعالى. فهي إذن أربعة أقطاب:
القطب الأول: النظر في ذات الله تعالى. فنبين فيه وجوده وانه قديم  وأنه
باق وأنه ليس بجوهر ولا جسم ولا عرض ولا محدود بحد ولا هو مخصوص بجهة، وأنه
مرئي كما أنه معلوم وأنه واحد؛ فهذه عشرة دعاوى نبينها في هذا القطب.
القطب الثاني: في صفات الله تعالى. ونبين فيه أنه حي عالم قادر مريد سميع
بصير متكلم وأن له حياة وعلما وقدرة وإرادة وسمعا وبصرا وكلاما، ونذكر
أحكام هذه الصفات ولوازمها وما يفترق فيها وما يجتمع فيها من الأحكام، وأن
هذه الصفات زائدة على الذات وقديمة وقائمة بالذات ولا يجوز أن يكون شيء من
الصفات حادثا.
القطب الثالث: في أفعال الله تعالى. وفيه سبعة دعاوى وهو انه لا يجب على
الله تعالى التكليف ولا الخلق ولا الثواب على التكليف ولا رعاية صلاح
العباد ولا يستحيل منه تكليف ما لا يطاق ولا يجب عليه العقاب على المعاصي
ولا يستحيل منه بعثه الأنبياء عليهم السلام؛ بل يجوز ذلك. وفي مقدمة هذا
القطب بيان معنى الواجب والحسن والقبيح.
القطب الرابع: في رسل الله، وما جاء على لسان رسولنا محمد صلى الله عليه
وسلم من الحشر والنشر والجنة والنار والشفاعة وعذاب القبر والميزان
والصراط، وفيه أربعة أبواب: الباب الأول: في إثبات نبوة محمد صلى الله عليه
وسلم.
الباب الثاني: فيما ورد على لسانه من أمور الآخرة.
الباب الثالث: في الإمامة وشروطها.
الباب الرابع: في بيان القانون في تكفير الفرق المبتدعة.

### | التمهيد الأول في بيان أن

- Root: ق-ص-د (qa-ṣad)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: The middle path between two extremes; uprightness and moderation in aim.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The praiseworthy mean in belief and action, opposed to ifrāṭ (excess) and tafrīṭ (negligence).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal sense is "intention/aim"; here used metaphorically for the balanced theological method.
- Sībawayh Rule: ʿAṭf al-Bayān (Appositional explicative) — e.g., "عصابة الحق وأهل السنة" where the second phrase clarifies the first.
chapters.translation:
In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate.

Praise be to Allah, who chose from the elite of His servants the band of truth and the people of the Sunnah, and singled them out among all the sects with the favors of kindness and grace. He poured upon them from the light of His guidance that by which He unveiled the realities of religion, and He made their tongues speak with His proof by which He crushed the misguidance of the atheists. He purified their innermost consciences from the whisperings of the devils, and cleansed their hearts from the incitements of the deviant. He filled their hearts with the lights of certainty, until through them they were guided to the secrets of what He revealed upon the tongue of His Prophet and Chosen One, Muhammad — may Allah bless him and grant him peace — the master of the messengers. They came to see the way of reconciling between the requirements of the revealed laws and the dictates of the intellects, and they ascertained that there is no opposition between the transmitted Law (al-sharʿ al-manqūl) and the rational truth (al-ḥaqq al-maʿqūl).

They knew that those among the Ḥashwiyyah who deemed it obligatory to remain frozen in blind following (taqlīd) and adherence to literal appearances — they only arrived at this from weakness of intellects and paucity of insight. And those among the philosophers and the extremist Muʿtazilah who delved deep into the exercise of reason until they collided with it against the categorical proofs of the Law — they only arrived at this from the corruption of their inner consciences. The inclination of the former is toward negligence (tafrīṭ), and the inclination of the latter is toward excess (ifrāṭ), and both are far from prudence and caution. Rather, the obligatory and binding duty in the foundations of belief is adherence to moderation (iqtiṣād) and reliance upon the straight path; for both extremes in pursuing matters are blameworthy.

How can right guidance be secured for one who is content with blind following of tradition and report, and denies the methodologies of inquiry and reflection — or does not know that there is no basis for the Law except the word of the master of mankind, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and that the proof of reason is that by which his truthfulness is known in what he reported? And how can one be guided to correctness who pursues pure reason alone and restricts himself to it, without being illuminated by the light of the Law nor gaining insight? Would that I knew — how can one flee to reason when incapacity and perplexity afflict it? Or does he not know that reason is deficient and that its domain is narrow and confined? Far from it! He has certainly failed with absolute certainty and become entangled in the trails of misguidance — he who does not unite, through the composition of the Law and reason, this scattered disarray.

The example of reason is sound eyesight free from defects and harm. The example of the Qurʾān is the sun spreading its radiance. How fitting it is that the seeker of guidance be self-sufficient — but if he relies on one of them to the exclusion of the other, he is among the ranks of the foolish. For the one who turns away from reason, contenting himself with the light of the Qurʾān, his example is one who exposes himself to the sun's light while closing his eyelids — there is no difference between him and the blind. So reason with the Law is light upon light, and the one who looks with a squinting eye at either one specifically is clinging to a rope of delusion.

It will become clear to you, O aspirant yearning to examine the foundations of the creed of the people of the Sunnah, seeking to verify them by categorical proofs, that no group has been singled out for success in combining the Law and verification except this group. So thank Allah the Exalted for your following in their footsteps, your entry into the order of their system and their standard, and your mixing with their party; perhaps you will be gathered on the Day of Resurrection in their company. We ask Allah the Exalted to purify our innermost secrets from the turbidities of misguidance, and to flood them with the light of truth, and to silence our tongues from speaking falsehood, and to make them speak with truth and wisdom. Indeed, He is the Generous, the Abundant in favor, the Vast in mercy.

### | Chapter

Let us open the discourse with an explanation of the name of the book, and the division of its premises, chapters, and sections. As for the name of the book, it is *Moderation in Belief* (al-Iqtiṣād fī al-Iʿtiqād). As for its arrangement, it comprises four Premises (tamhīdāt) that serve as introductions and preliminaries, and four Poles (aqṭāb) that serve as the objectives and ends.

### | The First Premise: On the Explanation That

This science is among the important matters in religion.
The Second Premise: On the explanation that it is not important for all Muslims, but rather for a specific group among them.
The Third Premise: On the explanation that it is among the communal obligations (furūḍ al-kifāyāt), not individual obligations (furūḍ al-aʿyān).
The Fourth Premise: On the detailed exposition of the methodologies of the proofs that I have adduced in this book.

As for the intended Poles, they are four, and their totality is confined to reflection upon Allah the Exalted. For when we look at the world, we do not look at it insofar as it is a world, a body, a heaven, or an earth, but rather insofar as it is the handiwork of Allah, glorified be He. And when we look at the Prophet, peace be upon him, we do not look at him insofar as he is a human being, noble, learned, and virtuous, but rather insofar as he is the Messenger of Allah. And when we look at his statements, we do not look at them insofar as they are statements, addresses, and communications, but rather insofar as they are definitions (taʿrīfāt) from Allah the Exalted conveyed through him. So there is no reflection except upon Allah, and no object of seeking except Allah. All the branches of this science are encompassed by reflection upon the Essence of Allah the Exalted, upon His attributes, glorified be He, upon His acts, mighty be His majesty, and upon the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and what has come to us upon his tongue of the definitions of Allah the Exalted. These are therefore four Poles:

**The First Pole:** Reflection upon the Essence of Allah the Exalted. In it we demonstrate His existence, that He is eternal (qadīm), that He is everlasting (bāqī), that He is not a substance (jawhar), nor a body (jism), nor an accident (ʿaraḍ), nor limited by a boundary, nor particularized by a direction (jihah), that He is visible (marʾī) just as He is known, and that He is one (wāḥid). These are ten claims that we demonstrate in this Pole.

**The Second Pole:** On the attributes of Allah the Exalted. In it we demonstrate that He is living (ḥayy), knowing (ʿālim), powerful (qādir), willing (murīd), hearing (samīʿ), seeing (baṣīr), and speaking (mutakallim), and that He has life (ḥayāh), knowledge (ʿilm), power (qudrah), will (irādah), hearing (samʿ), sight (baṣar), and speech (kalām). We mention the rulings of these attributes, their necessary concomitants (lawāzim), wherein they differ and wherein they agree in their rulings, and that these attributes are additional to the Essence (zāʾidah ʿalā al-dhāt), eternal (qadīmah), and subsisting in the Essence (qāʾimah bi al-dhāt), and that it is not permissible for any of the attributes to be originated (ḥādith).

**The Third Pole:** On the acts of Allah the Exalted. In it there are seven claims: that it is not obligatory upon Allah the Exalted to impose obligation (taklīf), nor to create, nor to reward for obligation, nor to observe the welfare (ṣalāḥ) of the servants; that it is not impossible for Him to obligate what is beyond one's capacity (taklīf mā lā yuṭāq); that it is not obligatory upon Him to punish for disobedience; and that it is not impossible for Him to send the prophets, peace be upon them — rather, that is permissible (jāʾiz). In the introduction to this Pole is the explanation of the meaning of the obligatory (wājib), the good (ḥasan), and the evil (qabīḥ).

**The Fourth Pole:** On the messengers of Allah, and what has come upon the tongue of our Messenger Muhammad, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, concerning the gathering (ḥashr), the resurrection (nashr), paradise (jannah), the fire (nār), intercession (shafāʿah), the punishment of the grave (ʿadhāb al-qabr), the scale (mīzān), and the path (ṣirāṭ). In it there are four chapters: The First Chapter: On establishing the prophethood of Muhammad, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. The Second Chapter: On what has been reported upon his tongue concerning the matters of the Hereafter. The Third Chapter: On the imamate (imāmah) and its conditions. The Fourth Chapter: On the explanation of the principle (qānūn) for declaring the innovating sects to be unbelievers (takfīr).

### | الخوض في هذا العلم مهم في الدين

اعلم أن صرف الهمة إلى ما ليس بمهم، وتضييع الزمان بما عنه بد هو غاية
الضلال ونهاية الخسران سواء كان المنصرف إليه بالهمة من العلوم أو من
الأعمال، فنعوذ بالله من علم لا ينفع. وأهم الأمور لكافة الخلق نيل السعادة
الأبدية واجتناب الشقاوة الدائمة، وقد ورد الأنبياء وأخبروا الخلق بأن لله
تعالى على عباده حقوقا ووظائف في أفعالهم وأقوالهم وعقائدهم. وأن من لم
ينطق بالصدق لسانه ولم ينطو على الحق ضميره ولم تتزين بالعدل جوارحه فمصيره
إلى النار وعاقبته للبوار. ثم لم يقتصروا  على مجرد الإخبار بل استشهدوا على
صدقهم بأمور غريبة وأفعال عجيبة خارقة للعادات خارجة عن مقدورات البشر، فمن
شاهدها أو سمع أحوالها بالأخبار المتواترة سبق إلى عقله إمكان صدقهم، بل
غلب على ظنه ذلك بأول السماع قبل أن يمعن النظر في تمييز المعجزات عن عجائب
الصناعات. وهذا الظن البديهي أو التجويز الضروري ينزع الطمأنينة عن القلب
ويحشوه بالاستشعار والخوف ويهيجه للبحث والافتكار ويسلب عنه الدعة والقرار
ويحذره مغبة التساهل والإهمال ويقرر عنده أن الموت آت لا محالة وأن ما بعد
الموت منطو عن أبصار الخلق وأن ما أخبر به هؤلاء غير خارج عن حيز الإمكان.
فالحزم ترك التواني في الكشف عن حقيقة هذا الأمر. فما هؤلاء مع العجائب
التي أظهروها في إمكان صدقهم قبل البحث عن تحقيق قولهم بأقل من شخص واحد
يخبرنا عن خروجنا من دارنا ومحل استقرارنا بأن سبعا من السباع قد دخل الدار
فخذ حذرك واحترز منه لنفسك جهدك، فإنا بمجرد السماع إذا رأينا ما أخبرنا
عنه في محل الامكان والجواز لم نقدم على الدخول وبالغنا في الاحتراز فالموت
هو المستقر والوطن قطعا، فكيف لا يكون الاحتراز لما بعده مهما؟ فإذن أهم
الممات أن نبحث عن قوله الذي قضى الذهن في بادئ الرأي وسابق النظر بامكانه
أهو محال في نفسه على التحقيق أو هو حق لا شك فيه؟ فمن
قوله ان لكم ربا كلفكم حقوقا وهو يعاقبكم على تركها ويثيبكم على فعلها
وقد بعثني رسولا إليكم لأبين ذلك لكم، فيلزمنا لا محالة أن نعرف أن لنا ربا
أم لا. وإن كان فهل يمكن أن يكون حيا متكلما حتى يأمر وينهى ويكلف ويبعث
الرسل، وإن كان متكلما فهل هو قادر على أن يعاقب ويثيب إذا عصيناه أو
أطعناه، وإن كان قادرا فهل هذا الشخص بعينه صادق في قوله أنا الرسول إليكم.
فإن اتضح لنا ذلك لزمنا لا محالة، إن كنا عقلاء، أن نأخذ حذرنا وننظر
لأنفسنا ونستحقر هذه الدنيا المنقرضة بالاضافة إلى الآخرة الباقية فالعاقل
من ينظر لعاقبته  ولا يغتر بعاجلته. ومقصود هذا العلم إقامة البرهان على
وجود الرب تعالى وصفاته وأفعاله وصدق الرسل كما فصلناه في الفهرست. وكل ذلك
مهم لا محيص عنه لعاقل.
فإن قلت اني لست منكرا هذا الانبعاث للطلب من نفسي ولكني لست أدري أنه
ثمرة الجبلة والطبع وهو مقتضى العقل أو هو موجب الشرع إذ للناس كلام في
مدارك الوجوب؛ فهذا انما تعرفه في آخر الكتاب عند تعرضنا لمدارك الوجوب.
والاشتغال به الآن فضول بل لا سبيل بعد وقوع الانبعاث إلى الانتهاض لطلب
الخلاص. فمثال الملتفت إلى ذلك مثال رجل لدغته حية أو عقرب وهي معاودة
اللدغ والرجل قادر على الفرار ولكنه متوقف ليعرف ان الحية جاءته من جانب
اليمين أو من جانب اليسار، وذلك من أفعال الأغبياء الجهال نعوذ بالله من
الاشتغال بالفضول مع تضييع المهمات والأصول.

chapters.anchors:
- Root: ه-م-م (h-m-m)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Core meaning of "concern, intention, or that which occupies one's resolve"; al-himmah is the directing of one's aspiration toward a goal.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In theological usage, himmah denotes the soul's earnest striving toward what pertains to its ultimate felicity (saʿādah) or ruin (shaqāwah), distinguishing the essential from the superfluous.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) — the heart's inclination to a matter; metaphorical (majāz) — wasting himmah on the non-essential is likened to squandering one's very life-capital.
- Root: خ-ر-ق (kh-r-q)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To tear or rend; kharq al-ʿādah — the rending of habitual course, i.e., miracle.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Technical term for miracles (muʿjizāt) as divine acts breaking natural custom, establishing prophetic veracity.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal — tearing a garment; metaphorical — the supernatural breach of ordinary causality, perceptible to the rational mind as possible (imkān).
- Root: ح-ز-م (ḥ-z-m)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Prudence, firm resolve, taking precautions against harm.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The rational virtue of acting upon probable danger; in kalām, it is the practical imperative to investigate matters of ultimate consequence.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal — binding a thing tightly; metaphorical — binding oneself to cautious action in the face of credible threat.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional and Exceptive Constructions (al-sharṭ wa al-istithnāʾ) — The text employs layered conditionals (fa-in qulta..., fa-in ittaḍaḥa...) and exceptions (lā maḥālah, lā ḥayṣ) to structure the argument's logical inevitability, requiring precise parsing of protasis and apodosis for faithful rendering.

### | Engaging in This Science Is Important in Religion

Know that directing one's concern toward what is not important, and wasting time upon that from which one is free, is the extreme of error and the end of loss — whether that to which one directs one's concern be of the sciences or of the deeds. We seek refuge in God from knowledge that does not benefit. And the most important of matters for all creatures is the attainment of eternal felicity (saʿādah) and the avoidance of perpetual misery (shaqāwah). The prophets came and informed creation that God — exalted be He — has rights and obligations upon His servants in their deeds, their words, and their beliefs; and that whoever's tongue does not utter truth, whose conscience does not embrace righteousness, and whose limbs are not adorned with justice — his end is the Fire and his consequence is ruin. Then they did not confine themselves to mere informing, but bore witness to their truthfulness through extraordinary matters and wondrous acts that break habitual customs (khawāriq al-ʿādāt) and exceed human capacities. Whoever witnessed them, or heard of their reports through successive transmission (tawātur), the possibility of their truthfulness springs to his mind — nay, it prevails upon his conjecture at the very first hearing, before he deeply examines the distinction between miracles (muʿjizāt) and the wonders of artifice. This intuitive conjecture or necessary allowance (tajwīz ḍarūrī) strips tranquility from the heart, fills it with apprehension and fear, rouses it to investigation and reflection, robs it of ease and rest, warns it of the consequence of negligence and heedlessness, and establishes within it that death is inevitably coming, that what lies after death is veiled from the eyes of creatures, and that what these [prophets] have reported is not outside the realm of possibility. Prudence (ḥazm), therefore, is to abandon procrastination in uncovering the reality of this matter. For these [prophets], with the wonders they have displayed, are not less in the possibility of their truthfulness — before investigating the verification of their claim — than a single person who informs us of our departure from our house and place of settlement, saying that a beast of prey has entered the dwelling: "Take your guard and protect yourself from it with all your effort." For we, upon mere hearing, when we see what we have been informed of to be within the realm of possibility and permissibility, do not proceed to enter, and we are extreme in our caution. So death is the resting place and the homeland, certainly — how then should caution for what follows it not be of the utmost importance? Therefore, the most important of important matters is that we investigate his claim — concerning which the mind has already judged, at first glance and initial consideration, its possibility — whether it is in itself impossible upon verification, or whether it is true beyond doubt. For he says: "You have a Lord who has charged you with obligations, who punishes you for abandoning them and rewards you for performing them, and He has sent me as a messenger to you to make this clear to you." It necessarily follows for us, without any escape, that we know whether we have a Lord or not. And if there is one, is it possible that He is living and speaking (ḥayy, mutakallim) such that He commands and forbids, imposes obligations, and sends messengers? And if He is speaking, is He able to punish and reward if we disobey Him or obey Him? And if He is able, is this very person truthful in his claim, "I am the messenger to you"? For if this becomes clear to us, it necessarily follows — if we are rational — that we take our guard, look to ourselves, and deem this passing world contemptible in comparison to the abiding Hereafter. For the rational person is one who looks to his ultimate consequence and is not deluded by his immediate present. And the purpose of this science is the establishment of demonstration (burhān) upon the existence of the Lord — exalted be He — His attributes, His acts, and the truthfulness of the messengers, as we have detailed in the index. And all of that is important, with no escape from it for any rational being.

If you say: "I do not deny this arousal to seek within myself, but I do not know whether it is the fruit of innate disposition (jibillah) and nature, being a requirement of reason, or whether it is an obligation of the Law (sharʿ) — for people have discourse concerning the sources of obligation (madārik al-wujūb)" — then this you will only know at the end of the book, when we address the sources of obligation. To occupy oneself with it now is superfluous — nay, there is no way, after the arousal has occurred, to delay in rising to seek deliverance. For the example of one who turns to that is like a man stung by a serpent or scorpion while it continues to strike, and the man is able to flee, yet he pauses to know whether the serpent came to him from the right side or the left side — and that is among the acts of the stupid and ignorant. We seek refuge in God from occupying oneself with the superfluous while squandering the important matters and the fundamentals.
